reference: Contract values in the output layout of sysstat 12.7.5 iostat and procps-ng pmap as observed by running both programs on Debian 13 (black-box; no source consulted). Numbers are computed independently from the kernel's diskstats and stat field definitions (docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/iostats.html, proc(5)); the banner is matched by shape because it names the running kernel, host and date.
coverage: G84: iostat -c, -d, -x, plain iostat, device order and selection, missing diskstats and usage errors.
G84: procps pmap header, row layout, mapping names and total, including a kernel thread's [comm] header.
exclusions: Interval and count operands (repeated reports) are not implemented; each report is the since-boot average.
pmap -x keeps bash-os's offset column rather than procps's RSS/Dirty columns, which need smaps.

cases.purpose: G84: iostat -c prints sysstat's banner (kernel, node, date, machine, CPU count from the cpuN lines) and the avg-cpu report, %system being system+irq+softirq over a total that leaves guest time out, followed by sysstat's three blank lines.
cases.script:
mkdir -p proc
printf 'cpu 100 20 30 400 10 5 5 0 10 2\ncpu0 50 0 10 40 0 0 0 0 0 0\ncpu1 50 20 20 360 10 5 5 0 10 2\nintr 99\n' > proc/stat
b=$(BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=proc procstat iostat -c | head -2)
[[ $b =~ ^[^\ ]+\ [^\ ]+\ \(.*\)\ $'\t'[^\ ]+\ $'\t'_[^\ ]+_$'\t'\(2\ CPU\)$ ]] && echo banner-ok
BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=proc procstat iostat -c | tail -n +3

cases.purpose: G84: sysstat lists devices by name, not in diskstats order; an alternate proc tree without BASHOS_SYS_ROOT keeps every device with I/O.
cases.script:

printf '%s\n' '259 0 nvme0n1 1 0 2 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0' '8 0 md0 1 0 2 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0' > proc/diskstats

cases.script:

cases.purpose: G84: an option iostat does not implement is a usage error with no report.

G84: pmap prints procps's 'PID:   COMMAND ARGS' header from cmdline, rows of a 16-digit address, a 6-column size with K, a five-column mode with the shared flag fourth, and the mapping's base name or [ stack ]/[ anon ], then ' total' with the size in 16 columns.
cases.script:
mkdir -p proc/7
printf 'sleep\0' > proc/7/cmdline
printf 'sleep\n' > proc/7/comm
printf '%s\n' '400000-402000 r-xp 00000000 08:01 9 /usr/bin/sleep' '600000-601000 rw-s 00000000 00:05 3 /dev/zero (deleted)' '7ff000-800000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0 [stack]' '900000-904000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0' > proc/7/maps
BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=proc procstat pmap 7

cases.purpose: G84: a process with an empty cmdline (a kernel thread) is named [comm] in the header, as procps does; with neither file the header is 'PID:'.
cases.script:
mkdir -p proc/2 proc/3
: > proc/2/cmdline
printf 'kthreadd\n' > proc/2/comm
: > proc/2/maps
: > proc/3/maps
BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=proc procstat pmap 2 3
